name: CardioXplorer
full_name: CardioXplorer open-source modular teleoperated robotic catheter-ablation system
group: King's College London, School of Biomedical Engineering & Imaging Sciences (K. S. Rhode, R. J. Housden; Z. Xu, A. M. Zeidan) with Guy's and St Thomas' and St George's hospitals
versions: 2024 MDPI Robotics (only); sibling KCL robot for transseptal puncture (kcl_tsp_zeidan2023)
devices_driven: commercial ablation catheters through a catheter-agnostic handle gripper: Thermocool SmartTouch SF and CS, Webster CS EZ Steer (Biosense Webster), Blazer II XP (Boston Scientific) (Sec. 2.1)
translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp (linear module: NEMA-17 stepper with GT2 belt drive carries the handle, 220 mm insertion depth)
rotation_detail: NEMA-8 stepper (19:1) rotates the handle without limit through a slip ring; servo (12 kg.cm holding torque) turns the knob +-60 deg
device_range: four commercial ablation catheter models (open-source CAD handles)
force_sensing: none on the robot (knob torque of about 6 kg.cm measured during design)
imaging_compat: NDI Aurora EM tracking in tests; phantom imaged on a Siemens Artis Q biplane
sterility: detachable disposable single-use catheter; N.R. further
validation_detail: benchtop targeting of left pulmonary veins in an AF-patient cardiac phantom; 3 cardiologists and 2 trainees, 5 trials, manual vs robot (Sec. 3)
key_numbers: task duration -1.59 s with the robot; robotic motion 35.2% smoother for experts than intermediates; jerk improvement vs manual 42.2% (experts) and 13.6% (intermediates); speeds up to +-25 mm/s, 0.5 deg rotation steps up to 9.375 rps; parts cost about USD 700 (abstract, Sec. 2)
